concerns.text: Terminology drift for the same target variable: FR-002 says 'predict the ACE-Ego-0 ground-truth reliability scores' while FR-003 says 'residual error between the static model predictions and the actual dynamic reliability scores'. Pick one term (e.g., 'ground-truth (dynamic) reliability scores') and use it consistently so FR-002/FR-003 unambiguously refer to the same quantity.

Edge Cases state missing features are handled by 'imputing with dataset mean OR excluding the segment, logging the exclusion count', but the Assumptions section commits only to 'the system will impute with the dataset mean'. These two fallback policies should be reconciled (e.g., state imputation is primary and exclusion is the fallback) so implementers know which behavior is required.

FR-005 requires evaluation on 'RoboCasa and RoboTwin benchmarks' (both), but US-3 Acceptance Scenario 1 only exercises RoboCasa ('evaluates the model on the RoboCasa benchmark'). RoboTwin evaluation is never exercised by any acceptance scenario; either add it to the scenario or note the scope difference explicitly.

FR-007 says the threshold is 'based on the static model's confidence', while the idea's methodology says 'predicted to be low-fidelity or where the static model's uncertainty is high' — two different signals (predicted score vs. model uncertainty). Also FR-002 offers 'Random Forest or shallow MLP', and neither is specified to produce a confidence output. Specify which signal (predicted reliability score, model uncertainty, or both) drives FR-007's threshold.
